title: LexInfo + OntoLex-Lemon Schema Terms

# LexInfo + OntoLex-Lemon Schema Terms

This MASP Schema was auto-generated from three merged ontologies using the `scripts/owl-to-masp.py` script (see spec: "Merging multiple ontologies into one schema"): the [LexInfo ontology](https://lexinfo.net/) (v3.0), and the [OntoLex-Lemon](https://www.w3.org/2016/05/ontolex/) `ontolex` (core) and `synsem` modules that LexInfo's own properties specialise. Converting all three together, rather than as three separate schemas, means classes like `ontolex:LexicalEntry` and `ontolex:LexicalSense` — which many LexInfo properties point at as their domain — resolve to real, documented classes here instead of bare external IRIs.

The ontologies' named individuals (e.g. the `lexinfo:PartOfSpeech` values `lexinfo:noun`, `lexinfo:verb`, or the `lexinfo:Case`, `lexinfo:Gender` and `lexinfo:Tense` values) are ported as instances of their class and listed in an `ItemList` per class. Properties whose range is one of those classes (e.g. `lexinfo:partOfSpeech`) offer the standard values from that list, but keep the class in their range too, so other instances of the class are still valid.

### <a id="RootMorph" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#RootMorph"></a> Class: morphological root <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#RootMorph)</small>

A root is the portion of a word that (a) is common to a set of derived or inflected forms, (b) is not further analyzable into meaningful elements, and (c) carries the principle portion of meaning of the words in which it functions (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/root).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

### <a id="SimulfixMorph" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#SimulfixMorph"></a> Class: simulfix <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#SimulfixMorph)</small>

A simulfix is a change or replacement of vowels or consonants (usually vowels) which changes the meaning of a word (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/simulfix). Examples include umlaut in Germanic languages, e.g., in the formation of the English plural feet from the singular foot.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="StemMorph" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#StemMorph"></a> Class: morphological stem <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#StemMorph)</small>

A stem is the root or roots of a word, together with any derivational affixes, to which inflectional affixes are added (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/stem). A stem consists minimally of a root, but may be analyzable into a root plus derivational morphemes.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="TransfixMorph" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#TransfixMorph"></a> Class: transfix <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#TransfixMorph)</small>

A transfix is a discontinuous affix that disrupts the base to which it is attached. The term is reserved for true single affixes, rather than combinations of an infix with an independent prefix or suffix. (Broselow, E., 2000. Transfixation. In G. Booij, et al. (eds.), Ein internationales Handbuch zur Flexion und Wortbildung. 1. Halbband. Mouton De Gruyter, New York, Berlin, p. 552-557.) Examples include discontinuous affixes inserted into a word root, as in root-and-pattern systems of several Semitic languages, e.g., in the Arabic word kitaba "writing" from the root k-t-b.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="ZeroMorph" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#ZeroMorph"></a> Class: zero morph <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#ZeroMorph)</small>

A zero morph is a morph, consisting of no phonetic form, that is proposed in some analyses as an allomorph of a morpheme that is ordinarily realized by a morph having some phonetic form (as defined by the SIL Glossary of Linguistic Terms, https://glossary.sil.org/term/zero-morph). Examples include the English plural sheep along with the singular sheep.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from zero morph

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="Affix" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#Affix"></a> Class: affix <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#Affix)</small>

An affix is a lexical entry that represents a morpheme (suffix, prefix, infix, circumfix) that is attached to a word stem to form a new word.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

*No properties defined directly on this class*

### <a id="LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry"></a> Class: lexical entry <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry)</small>

A lexical entry represents a unit of analysis of the lexicon that consists of a set of forms that are grammatically related and a set of base meanings that are associated with all of these forms. Thus, a lexical entry is a word, multiword expression or affix with a single part-of-speech, morphological pattern, etymology and set of senses.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |

| <a href="#acronymFor" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#acronymFor">acronymFor</a> | No | A linking element used to identify a relation between an acronym and its full or expanded form. | <a href="#LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry">lexical entry</a> |  |
| <a href="#canonicalForm" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#canonicalForm">canonicalForm</a> | No | The 'canonical form' property relates a lexical entry to its canoncical or dictionary form. | <a href="#clippedTermFor" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#clippedTermFor">clippedTermFor</a> | No | A linking element used to identify a relation between a clipped term and its full or expanded form. | <a href="#LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry">lexical entry</a> |  |
| <a href="#contractionFor" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#contractionFor">contractionFor</a> | No | The full form that corresponds to a contracted form. | <a href="#LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry">lexical entry</a> |  |
| <a href="#denotes" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#denotes">denotes</a> | No | The 'denotes' property relates a lexical entry to a predicate in a given ontology that represents its meaning and has some denotational or model-theoretic semantics.  | <a href="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource" title="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Resource</a> |  |
| <a href="#derivedForm" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#derivedForm">derivedForm</a> | No | A form that is derived morphosyntactically from another form | <a href="#LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry">lexical entry</a> |  |

| <a href="#initialismFor" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#initialismFor">initialismFor</a> | No | A linking element used to identify a relation between an initialism and its full or expanded form. | <a href="#LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry">lexical entry</a> |  |

| <a href="#morphologicalPattern" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#morphologicalPattern">morphologicalPattern</a> | No | The 'morphological pattern' property indicates the morphological class of a word. |  |  |

| <a href="#shortFormFor" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#shortFormFor">shortFormFor</a> | No | A linking element used to identify a relation between a short form and its full or expanded form. | <a href="#LexicalEntry" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalEntry">lexical entry</a> |  |

### <a id="LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense"></a> Class: lexical sense <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense)</small>

A lexical sense represents the lexical meaning of a lexical entry when interpreted as referring to the corresponding ontology element. A lexical sense thus represents a reification of a pair of a uniquely determined lexical entry and a uniquely determined ontology entity it refers to. A link between a lexical entry and an ontology entity via a Lexical Sense object implies that the lexical entry can be used to refer to the ontology entity in question.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from lexical sense

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#antonym" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#antonym">antonym</a> | No | A term or lexeme whose concept or sense constitutes the opposite of the concept represented by a second term or lexeme. | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#approximate" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#approximate">approximate</a> | No | Property used to qualify something similar but not exactly the same | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#approximateSynonym" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#approximateSynonym">approximateSynonym</a> | No | A synonym that differs in some minor way | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#associativeRelation" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#associativeRelation">associativeRelation</a> | No | A relation between two concepts having a non-hierarchical thematic connection by virtue of experience. | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#causallyRelatedConcept" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#causallyRelatedConcept">causallyRelatedConcept</a> | No | A concept that is related to another concept by virtue of the fact that it plays a causative role with respect to that concept. | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#collocation" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#collocation">collocation</a> | No | Two terms that occur together far more frequently than chance | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#coordinateConcept" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#coordinateConcept">coordinateConcept</a> | No | A subordinate concept having the same nearest superordinate concept and same criterion of subdivision as some other concept in a given concept system. | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |

| <a href="#holonymTerm" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#holonymTerm">holonymTerm</a> | No | Indicates that the referenced element is a part of this object | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#hypernym" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#hypernym">hypernym</a> | No | A term with a broader meaning | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#hyponym" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#hyponym">hyponym</a> | No | A term with a narrower meaning | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |

| <a href="#partMeronym" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#partMeronym">partMeronym</a> | No | Indicates this a component of the other concept | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#partitiveRelation" title="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#partitiveRelation">partitiveRelation</a> | No | A relation between two concepts where one of the concepts constitutes the whole and the other concept a part of that whole. | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |

### <a id="OntoMap" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#OntoMap"></a> Class: ontology mapping <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#OntoMap)</small>

An 'ontology mapping' (OntoMap for short) specifies how a syntactic frame and its syntactic arguments map to a set of concepts and properties in the ontology that together specify the meaning of the syntactic frame.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from ontology mapping

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#condition" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#condition">condition</a> | No | The 'condition' property defines an evaluable constraint that derives from using a certain lexical entry to express a given ontological predicate. |  |  |
| <a href="#ontoCorrespondence" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#ontoCorrespondence">ontoCorrespondence</a> | No | The 'ontoCorrespondence' property binds an argument of a predicate defined in the ontology to a syntactic argument that realizes this predicate argument syntactically. | <a href="#SyntacticArgument" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticArgument">Syntactic Argument</a> |  |
| <a href="#ontoMapping" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#ontoMapping">ontoMapping</a> | No | The 'ontoMapping' property relates an ontology mapping to its corresponding lexical sense. | <a href="#LexicalSense" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#LexicalSense">lexical sense</a> |  |
| <a href="#reference" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/ontolex#reference">reference</a> | No | The 'reference' property relates a lexical sense to an ontological predicate that represents the denotation of the corresponding lexical entry.  | <a href="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource" title="http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#Resource" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Resource</a> |  |
| <a href="#submap" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#submap">submap</a> | No | The 'submap' property relates a (complex) ontological mapping to a set of bindings that together bind the arguments of the involved predicates to a set of syntactic arguments that realize them syntactically. | <a href="#OntoMap" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#OntoMap">ontology mapping</a> |  |


### <a id="SyntacticArgument" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticArgument"></a> Class: Syntactic Argument <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticArgument)</small>

A 'syntactic argument' represents a slot that needs to be filled for a certain syntactic frame to be complete. Syntactic arguments typically realize a certain grammatical function (e.g. subject, direct object, indirect object, prepositional object, etc.).

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from Syntactic Argument

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#marker" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#marker">marker</a> | No | The 'marker' property indicates the marker of a syntactic argument; this can be a case marker or some other lexical entry such as a preposition or particle. |  |  |
| <a href="#optional" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#optional">optional</a> | No | The 'optional' property indicates whether a syntactic argument is optional, that is, it can be syntactically omitted. | schema:Boolean |  |


### <a id="SyntacticFrame" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticFrame"></a> Class: Syntactic Frame <small style="color:#aaa">(http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticFrame)</small>

A 'syntactic frame' represents the syntactic behavior of an open class word in terms of the (syntactic) arguments it requires. It essentially describes the so called subcategorization structure of the word in question, in particular the syntactic arguments it requires.

Instances of this type MAY be present in the crate.

| Min Count | Max Count |
| --------- | --------- |
| N/A | N/A |

#### Properties from Syntactic Frame

| Property | Required | Description | Range | Value |
| -------- | -------- | ----------- | ----- | ----- |
| <a href="#synArg" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#synArg">synArg</a> | No | The object property synArg relates a syntactic frame to one of its syntactic arguments. | <a href="#SyntacticArgument" title="http://www.w3.org/ns/lemon/synsem#SyntacticArgument">Syntactic Argument</a> |  |

  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses the meaning of presence &#39;at&#39; or &#39;near&#39; a place.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>aditive case</td><td><a id="aditiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#aditiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#aditiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#aditiveCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;aditive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case expressing &amp;quot;to&amp;quot; in Basque studies.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>allative case</td><td><a id="allativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#allativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#allativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#allativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;allative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses the meaning of motion &#39;to&#39; or &#39;towards&#39; the referent it marks.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>benefactive case</td><td><a id="benefactiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#benefactiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#benefactiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#benefactiveCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;benefactive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that expresses that the referent of the noun it marks receives the benefit of the situation expressed by the clause.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>causative case</td><td><a id="causativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#causativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#causativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#causativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;causative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses that the referent of the noun it marks is the cause of the situation expressed by the clause.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>comitative case</td><td><a id="comitativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#comitativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#comitativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#comitativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;comitative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses a meaning similar to &#39;along with&#39; or &#39;accompagnied by&#39;.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>dative case</td><td><a id="dativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#dativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#dativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#dativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;dative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that expresses an indirect object relationship or a range of meaning similar to that covered by &#39;to&#39; or &#39;for&#39; in English; but there is a great deal of variation between languages in the way this case is used.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>delative case</td><td><a id="delativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#delativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#delativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#delativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;delative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses motion downward from the referent of the noun it marks.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>direct case</td><td><a id="directCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#directCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#directCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#directCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;direct case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;An unmarked case which covers the single argument of a one-place verb and the agent and patient arguments of a transitive verb.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>elative case</td><td><a id="elativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#elativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#elativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#elativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;elative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses the meaning of motion &#39;away from&#39; from the referent of the noun it marks.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>equative case</td><td><a id="equativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#equativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#equativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#equativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;equative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that expresses likeness or identity to the referent of the noun it marks. It can have meaning, such as: &#39;as&#39;, &#39;like&#39;, or &#39;in the capacity of&#39;.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>ergative case</td><td><a id="ergativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#ergativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#ergativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#ergativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;ergative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case assigned to the subject of a transitive verb as opposed to absolutive case.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>essive case</td><td><a id="essiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#essiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#essiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#essiveCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;essive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses a state of being.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>genitive case</td><td><a id="genitiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#genitiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#genitiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#genitiveCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;genitive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses a possessive relationship (e.g. the boy&#39;s book) or some other similarly close connection (e.g. a summer&#39;s day).&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>illative case</td><td><a id="illativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#illativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#illativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#illativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;illative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses the meaning of &#39;motion into&#39; or &#39;direction towards&#39; the referent of the noun it marks.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>inessive case</td><td><a id="inessiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#inessiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#inessiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#inessiveCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;inessive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses the meaning of location or position within a place.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>instrumental case</td><td><a id="instrumentalCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#instrumentalCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#instrumentalCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#instrumentalCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;instrumental case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case indicating that the referent of the noun it marks is the means of the accomplishment of the action expressed by the clause.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>lative case</td><td><a id="lativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#lativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#lativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#lativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;lative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case which expresses motion to a location.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>locative case</td><td><a id="locativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#locativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#locativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;locative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that indicates a final location of action or a time of the action.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>nominative case</td><td><a id="nominativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#nominativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#nominativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#nominativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;nominative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case used to indicate the subject of a verb.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>oblique case</td><td><a id="obliqueCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#obliqueCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#obliqueCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#obliqueCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;oblique case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that is used when a noun is the object of a verb or a proposition, except for nominative and vocative case.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>partitive case</td><td><a id="partitiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#partitiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#partitiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;partitive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that expresses the partial nature of the referent of the noun it marks, as opposed to expressing the whole unit or class of which the referent is a part.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>prolative case</td><td><a id="prolativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#prolativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#prolativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;prolative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case for a noun or a pronoun that expresses motion within a place or a period of time needed for an event.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>sociative case</td><td><a id="sociativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#sociativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#sociativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;sociative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case related to the person in whose company the action is carried out, or to any belongings of people which take part in the action.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>sublative case</td><td><a id="sublativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#sublativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#sublativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;sublative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case for a move of something to the surface of another object.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>superessive case</td><td><a id="superessiveCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#superessiveCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#superessiveCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;superessive case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case indicating location on top of something or on the surface of something.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>terminative case</td><td><a id="terminativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#terminativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#terminativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#terminativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;terminative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case that indicates to what or where something ends.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>translative case</td><td><a id="translativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#translativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#translativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{
  &quot;@id&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#translativeCase&quot;,
  &quot;@type&quot;: &quot;http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#Case&quot;,
  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;translative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case indicating that the referent of the noun, or the quality of the adjective, that it marks is the result of a process of change.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
<tr><td>vocative case</td><td><a id="vocativeCase" href="http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#vocativeCase" target="_blank" rel="noopener">http://www.lexinfo.net/ontology/3.0/lexinfo#vocativeCase</a></td><td><pre><code>{

  &quot;name&quot;: &quot;vocative case&quot;,
  &quot;description&quot;: &quot;Case used to indicate direct address.&quot;
}</code></pre></td></tr>
</tbody></table>
